newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling edges up vs dlr, import demand fades.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling edges up vs dlr, import demand fades.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling gained slightly against the dollar on Wednesday as importer demand dwindled to a trickle in a calm market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.86 against the dollar from 55.88 on Tuesday. On the pound, shilling was posted at a mean of 88.66 from 88.35 on Tuesday.
"Shilling bulls continued to prevail in the market as importer demand dwindled to a trickle," a dealer said.
"The market opened at 55.83/93 and moved down by five cents barely one hour into the trading session, as players prepared to go short dollars," the dealer added.
"The central bank then came into the market and picked up about $3 million, sending the dollar back up to close at the same levels it opened at," he said.
A commercial banker said the shilling was stabilizing and forecast a gradual dollar depreciation the rest of the week as sentiment continued to favour the local unit.
Dealers said overnight money market remained at between 14 and 22 percent levels compared to 17-22 percent, previously.
